distractors.reason: We don't say 'work hardly'. 'Hardly' means 'almost not', so 'work hardly' would mean barely working.
We don't say 'work strongly'. 'Strongly' is used with opinions or feelings: strongly agree, strongly believe.
We don't say 'work heavily'. 'Heavily' is used with things like rain or drinking: heavily rain, heavily loaded.

example_sentence: Doctors and nurses work ___ every day.
l1_interference: Osoby mówiące po polsku często stawiają przysłówek przed czasownikiem, jak w 'ciężko pracować', i mogą powiedzieć 'hard work' zamiast poprawnego 'work hard'.
common_mistake: hard work (used instead of work hard)
explanation: In English, the adverb 'hard' comes after the verb 'work'. Think of 'work hard' as 'do the job with lots of effort'.

related_collocations.example: Students study hard before the exam.
Please listen carefully to the instructions.
The teacher speaks clearly so everyone understands.

memory_tip: HARD = with lots of effort (work hard, study hard) | HARDLY = almost not (I hardly see him)
